(2025) PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0316937 -- S1 File (Questionnaire, PDF, .s001) Part II for item wording, instructions and response anchors; S2 File (Minimal data set, XLSX, .s002) sheet 'Intercultural Competence Scores' for the column headers the IRW item codes were keyed from
note: The S2 workbook's column headers ARE the item wording (e.g. 'KN1-Knowledge of self-(1) understanding native history'), and data/yang_2025_intercultural.py maps each exact header string to its IRW code via an explicit name-keyed dict (AICCS_ITEMS) with an assertion that all 28 are present -- a name-keyed rename, not a positional assignment, so the code-to-text tie is made at the source. All 28 shipped item_text strings were re-checked as exact suffixes of their workbook headers (0 mismatches). Wording itself transcribed from S1 File Part II, which matches the headers verbatim; leading '(n) ' numbering and the dimension prefix were stripped, the dimension heading being carried in section_prompt instead (six section_ids, one per AIC-CCS dimension). instructions is Part II's framing paragraph plus its scale line, verbatim. option_text is S1's '(A) very low ... (E) very high' mapped ascending to 1-5; see public_note for the conflict with the article body's 'strongly disagree...strongly agree' description. Administration: questionnaire delivered via Wenjuanxing/WeChat to Chinese students in Ireland, but the published questionnaire (S1 File) is in English throughout and no Chinese wording appears in S1 or S2, so English is shipped as the administered wording and no language/_translated columns are emitted; only the semi-structured interviews are stated to have been conducted in Chinese. Rights: the AIC-CCS is Wu, Fan & Peng (2013), Foreign Language Teaching and Research 45(4):581-92 -- an academic journal scale with no test publisher; no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was locatable to quote, and IRW's copy comes from the CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE supplement that printed the full questionnaire. Silence is permission, so no rights block and no instrument_rights_register row written.
public_note: The response anchors shipped for yang_2025_aiccs are the questionnaire's own (A) very low / (B) low / (C) average / (D) high / (E) very high, taken from S1 File; the article's Methods section instead describes Sections II and III as running from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree), which does not fit these self-rating items

source_ref: Yang X, Nie Q (2026) PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0340479; S2 Data = pone.0340479.s002.xlsx (https://plos.figshare.com/articles/dataset/31284877), header row 2; per-item means for Q9-Q12 from the article's 'Learner attitudes and preferences on value integration' section (Table 5 text)
note: Item text is the study's own deposit header row (pone.0340479.s002.xlsx, row 2), which labels every one of the 36 columns; item codes are assigned positionally by data/yang2026_efl_learner_perspective.py (cols 7-42 -> item_01..item_36) and the mapping was re-run and reproduced cell-for-cell against live data (5544/5544 cells, 154 ids). CAVEATS: (1) option_text is blank for every item -- the deposit carries no value labels and the paper prints no response anchors, so no option wording exists to ship; the 0/1 items are select-all-that-apply checkboxes and 0/1 is selection status, not printed wording. (2) The four rating items (item_29..item_32) are stored in the OPPOSITE direction to the paper's reported scoring: the paper analyses a 4-point scale with 1=lowest and reports means 2.98/2.96/3.08/3.21, which reproduce as 5 - mean of the stored values over the >=35 s valid subset (2.993/2.971/3.081/3.213). So in the live table a LOWER value = stronger agreement. (3) The shipped wording is English; the survey was run on Wen Juan Xing with Chinese first-year non-English majors and was almost certainly administered in Chinese (the paper never states the language). The deposit contains zero CJK characters across all 44 columns including the free-text answers, and the only other supplement (S1 Data) is the textbook corpus, so the administered Chinese is not recoverable from the deposit or the paper's supplements -- hence text_source=translated_substitute with the authors' own English in the base fields. (4) Whitespace was collapsed and the wrapping parentheses stripped from the checkbox header cells (' (A. Patriotism) ' -> 'A. Patriotism'); questionnaire numbering ('3. ', '9. ') and option letters were kept as the source prints them. (5) Dictionary metadata is wrong about the paper: the reference reads 'Yang, X., Li, J., & Guo, K. (2026) ... Evidence from a survey of Chinese university students', but 10.1371/journal.pone.0340479 is Yang X & Nie Q (2026), 'Moral integration influences EFL oral English learning: Evidence from textbook analysis and learner feedback'. (6) No rights bar: the questionnaire is the study's own ad hoc instrument, not a published named scale, and it is distributed in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article's supporting information.
public_note: The four rating items (item_29-item_32) are stored with 1 = strongest agreement and 4 = weakest, the reverse of the 1=lowest/4=highest scoring the source paper reports; the paper's means 2.98/2.96/3.08/3.21 equal 5 minus the stored means. No response-option wording is shipped because neither the deposit nor the paper publishes anchors, and the 0/1 items are select-all-that-apply checkboxes where 1 = option selected.
